title: A Brief History of Paperwork
description: A 66-second mixed-media collage explainer: five thousand years of filling in the blanks, from clay receipts to AI. The worked example of the collage look (sketch/collage.js): copy it into projects/<id>/, then sketch-paint (17 cut-outs, ~$0.20), sketch-vo (Gemini, or --tts edge for free), score.py and sfx.py, sketch-audio, sketch-render.

vo.style: A warm, wry documentary narrator with a brisk, lively pace: clear and confident, with a smile in the voice, like a museum audio guide that enjoys its subject.

lines.text: Long before inboxes, there was paperwork.
Five thousand years ago, Mesopotamian scribes pressed receipts into clay: barley in, beer out.
In fourteen fifty-four, Mainz printed the first forms: indulgences, with blanks for a name.
By the eighteen-eighties, typewriters and carbon paper turned one form into three.
In nineteen thirteen, the first Form ten-forty ran four pages. Instructions included.
By the fifties, offices ran on filing cabinets and rubber stamps.
In nineteen ninety-three, the PDF put forms on screens. Soon you could type in the boxes.
By two thousand, a signature no longer needed ink.
Today, AI reads the form and fills in every field in seconds.
Five thousand years later, it's still paperwork. Just faster.
